candidate.answerReason: Similar tangent triangles locate the x-intercept at 8. A second similarity calculation gives the y-intercept exactly \(2\sqrt2\), so D is closest.

methods.label: Locate the intercept using similar triangles
methods.explanation:
The unequal radii suggest comparing the right triangles formed by the tangent and the line of centers.

Let \(A=(2,0)\) and \(B=(5,0)\) be the centers, and let \(T\) and \(U\) be their respective tangency points. The radii \(AT\) and \(BU\) are perpendicular to the tangent. Both point upward because the tangency points lie in the first quadrant, so the centers lie on the same side of the tangent.

The tangent cannot be vertical, since a vertical tangent to either circle touches it on the x-axis. It cannot be horizontal, since the two radii are different. Let its x-intercept be \(H=(q,0)\). Since the centers are on the same side of the line, \(q\) lies outside the interval from \(2\) to \(5\).

The right triangles \(HAT\) and \(HBU\) have the same angle at \(H\), so they are similar. Hence
\[
\frac{HA}{HB}=\frac{AT}{BU}=2.
\]
If \(q<2\), then \(HA<HB\), which is impossible. Therefore \(q>5\), and
\[
q-2=2(q-5),
\qquad q=8.
\]
Now \(HB=3\) and \(BU=1\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
HU=\sqrt{3^2-1^2}=\sqrt8.
\]
Let \(O=(0,0)\), and let \(Y\) be the y-intercept. The upper tangent slopes downward toward \(H\), so \(Y\) is above \(O\). Right triangles \(HOY\) and \(HUB\) share the angle at \(H\). Their corresponding legs give
\[
\frac{OY}{HO}=\frac{BU}{HU}=\frac1{\sqrt8}.
\]
Since \(HO=8\), the y-intercept is
\[
OY=\frac8{\sqrt8}=\boxed{2\sqrt2}.
\]
This equals choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\) exactly.
methods.levelReason: Similar right triangles and the Pythagorean theorem determine both intercepts without trigonometry or a point-to-line distance formula.
